clips.caption:
He sat across from Gorbachev and Schwarzkopf. Not reading about it later - in the room for it.

What he says he took from those rooms is simple and uncomfortable: whoever controls the flow of information holds the real power, and misinformation is just the other half of the same tool. Call something misinformation and you don't have to disprove it - you only have to make people stop looking at it.

That's not a one-time trick played on the news. It's the water you've been swimming in since before you could question it.

Comment RISE and I'll send you what he says they still don't want surfacing.

clips.caption:
Bill Clinton once said there's nothing at Groom Lake. No installation at Area 51. He says he had to say that - because it was classified, not because it was true.

That's the part that rarely gets said out loud: being made to lie, by design, so the official answer and the real answer can both exist pointed at the same question. Kevin ties it to today - the same machine that controlled that answer now runs social media too, deciding who gets banned and whose posts even reach you.

There's a word for the whole operation now. They call it misinformation.
